meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary jurisdiction; Luxembourg City as the corporate statutory seat and seat of the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic tradition) with direct application of EU Regulations and transposition of EU Directives in corporate, AML/CFT, and payment-services law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: DTA Luxembourg – People's Republic of China (signed 18 March 1994, in force 28 June 1995)
DTA Luxembourg – United States of America (1996 treaty, as amended by the 2009 Protocol, in force)
DTA Luxembourg – Hong Kong SAR (in force since 2008)
Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) joint bilateral investment treaties concluded with third states
EU-level international investment protection and trade agreements applicable in Luxembourg (e.g., CETA, EU-Japan EPA, EU-Korea FTA, EU-Chile Agreement)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (as amended), SARL Articles 180-190; Law of 27 October 2010 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended, including by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs - RBE) with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 22 February 2019; Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services (PSD2 transposition) governing the remittance-licence route; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT; CSSF Circular 18/654; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 December 2010 on the commercial register. Access to the RBE is restricted following the CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 (C-37/20 and C-601/20): competent authorities, obliged entities, and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest may access on a case-by-case basis. The EU AMLAR package (Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 and Directive (EU) 2024/1640) and the AMLA Regulation are effective as to institutional design and will apply fully from 10 July 2027.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Statuts) executed before a Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial act registered with the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Hague Apostille not required for internal Luxembourg use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card of each shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national registry of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Convention of 5 October 1961 (Luxembourg accession in force since 3 August 1979); alternatively consular legalization at the competent Luxembourg embassy or consulate where the issuing state is not a Hague Party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extrait de casier judiciaire (police and criminal record certificate) of each proposed director and senior officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial or prosecutorial authority of the person's country of ordinary residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable to the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or corporate extract of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official commercial or companies registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; consolidation by the RCSL where the corporate shareholder is itself Luxembourg-registered

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified bank reference with source-of-funds declaration for the initial capital contribution (minimum EUR 12,000 fully subscribed; 25% paid up at incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank of each subscriber or transferring financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-certified copy with Hague Apostille or consular legalization of the issuing state

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales, Articles 710-1 to 710-22 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif notarié (notarized deed of incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SARL minimum share capital EUR 12,000 fully subscribed and paid up before notarial execution; capital must be deposited in a blocked bank account in the company's name or into the notary's escrow account, evidenced by a bank certificate of payment presented to the notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED:
1. The share subscriptions reflected in the incorporation deed are hereby ratified, and the allotment of 12,000 fully-paid shares to the initial shareholders is confirmed.
2. The registered office at [Registered Office Address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, is adopted as the company’s statutory seat.
3. [Name] is appointed manager/manageress with sole signature authority; [Name] is appointed alternate manager where required.
4. The manager(s) are expressly authorised to open bank accounts, make declarations before the Luxembourg Business Registers, and prepare and submit regulatory licence applications, including the CSSF payment-institution application.
5. All actions already taken in furtherance of incorporation are ratified.
The Board remains responsible for ongoing compliance with the Law of 10 August 1915.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name check and draft constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name availability request to validate the proposed corporate name. Prepare the draft acte constitutif in consultation with a Luxembourg notary, and obtain a bank certificate confirming the blocking of the minimum share capital in a Luxembourg bank account or in the notary's escrow account.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and address
Draft acte constitutif
Identity documents of all shareholders
Bank certificate of payment/blockage of EUR 12,000
Lease agreement or written right to use the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or subject to a prior similar filing, promptly submit an amended name proposal and re-file the reservation/check request within 8 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All shareholders or their authorised attorneys appear before a Luxembourg notary. The notary verifies identity, capacity, and payment of capital, reads the draft articles, and has the parties execute the deed. The notary then authenticates the acte constitutif and issues certified copies for registration.
required_dossiers: Completed name availability confirmation
Passports or national ID cards of shareholders/managers
Power of attorney if any shareholder is not present
Bank certificate of share capital deposit
Draft articles of association
Proof of registered office availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or any party identifies an error in the deed, execute a supplemental notarial act rectifying the defective clauses before submission to the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified notarial deed and required statutory annexes through the RCS electronic filing system or at the LBR counter. Pay the official registration fee and obtain the Luxembourg registration number (numéro d'immatriculation). The RCS will verify the legal form, capital, managers, and registered office.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial acte constitutif
List of managers with specimen signatures (form E/02)
Consent of the entity occupying the registered office (form B/01 or similar)
Payment of RCS registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or deficiency notice, respond within 15 days by filing corrected forms or supplemental documents; failure to cure within the statutory period may require re-filing, with any additional fee paid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the electronic official gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) / LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the LBR automatically transmits the legal notice to RESA for publication. The publication is an important third-party publicity step and confirms the company's legal existence against third parties. No separate manual submission is normally needed after 2016 reforms, but the notary ensures the publication is effected.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number
Certified summary of the deed as prepared by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication contains errors, file a correction request with LBR and the notary within 10 days; notify third parties affected by the correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment permit and VAT registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction Générale des PME, and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the autorisation d'établissement (business permit) required for any commercial activity, including payment/remittance services. Simultaneously complete VAT registration with the AED using the Luxembourg business number. The permit application verifies the good repute and professional qualifications of the managers.
required_dossiers: RCS registration excerpt
Criminal record certificate (extrait de casier judiciaire) for managers
Professional qualifications or evidence of competence
Business plan and description of activity
VAT registration form (Formulaire 1)
Proof of registered office and liability insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry refuses or requests further information, submit a detailed reply within the set deadline or file an appeal before the Administrative Tribunal within one month of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon incorporation and establishment permit, file a comprehensive licence application under the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services. The application must evidence robust AML/CFT controls, governance, capital, business plan, outsourcing/payment-rail arrangements, and the fitness of board members and the AML compliance officer.
required_dossiers: Completed CSSF application form and electronic questionnaire
Articles of association and RCS excerpt
Business plan with 3-year financial projections
AML/CFT and know-your-customer policy
Organisational chart and governance manual
CVs, criminal records, and good-repute evidence for directors/managers
Ownership structure and proof of source of funds
Cross-border remittance rail contracts and correspondent/cash-pickup agreements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CSSF sends a clarification letter or requests additional documents, respond fully within the stated grace period; if authorisation is refused, submit a written defence and ultimately appeal to the administrative courts within 3 months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for payment institution authorisation; Ministère de l'Économie – Direction Générale des PME for business establishment permit
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Agrément en qualité d'établissement de paiement (Payment Institution Licence) under the Law of 10 November 2009; Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) under the Law of 2 September 2011

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No EIA required – Office-based remittance services are excluded from Annexes I and II of the Luxembourg environmental impact assessment law (Law of 15 May 2018); registration not required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, process effluents, or VOC emissions; office waste and electronic equipment waste are managed under municipal collection and Luxembourg WEEE regulations; stormwater discharge is uncontaminated and limited to sanitary/public drainage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certificate from the municipal fire authority and the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS); structural and building-occupancy approval from the Commune of the registered office; workplace safety and occupational health clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax (CIT) and municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal); integrated digital portal via MyGuichet.lu / Guichet.lu and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon notarial incorporation and registration of the SARL with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), the entity is automatically assigned a 14-digit national identification number (matricule) which serves as the corporate tax reference. VAT registration is perfected by submitting the electronic registration form (Formulaire 640 – inscription à la TVA) through MyGuichet to the AEDT, which issues a LU-prefixed VAT identification number (LU + 8 digits). Simultaneously, employer withholding tax registration is filed with the ACD and, where applicable, social security registration with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS). For the remittance/payment services scope, the CSSF payment-institution license dossier (Law of 10 November 2009) references the same matricule and VAT number, and AML/CFT registration is consolidated under the single corporate identity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; the SARL is per se a fully taxable resident corporation (CIT, municipal business tax, net wealth tax, and solidarity surcharge). Available elections include: (i) VAT grouping election under Article 59bis of the VAT Law (form a single taxable person with ≥90% controlled Luxembourg entities); (ii) fiscal integration for CIT purposes under Article 164bis LIR (95% direct/indirect Luxembourg-resident subsidiaries, 5-year confirmation commitment); (iii) IP box election under Article 50bis LIR (80% exemption of qualifying IP income, with election to apply per-scheme); (iv) the flat-rate cost election and joint taxation elections for closely held holding structures (SOPARFI). Hybrid mismatch positions are governed by the ATAD anti-hybrid rules (Article 168quater LIR), which create mandatory disallowance and do not grant an elective carve-out; the entity must file annual form 602 with the AEDT for cross-border restructuring events.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA – taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, transposing EU Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the small-enterprise exemption (Article 57 of the VAT Law); mandatory VAT registration is triggered from the moment taxable turnover exceeds this threshold (no threshold for non-established suppliers making taxable supplies).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory API stamping, or fiscal data transmission applies to B2B/B2C invoices; electronic invoicing is permitted and legally equivalent to paper. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only for B2G supplies (public procurement) via the PEPPOL network. All invoices issued by a Luxembourg SARL must bear the tax identification number and comply with the VAT invoice content requirements (Articles 57–59 of the VAT Law). Because the activity is cross-border remittance (payment transactions), PSPs are subject to the CESOP/DAC7 reporting framework requiring quarterly reporting of cross-border payment data to the Luxembourg tax authorities (first transmission by 31 January 2025).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: 0% VAT applies (Article 53 of the VAT Law) where goods are physically exported outside the EU, evidenced by transport/dispatch proof and a customs export declaration (SAD) accepted within 90 days of the supply date. For services: the remittance and payment-transfer services at issue are VAT-exempt without right to deduction (Article 44(1)(c) of the VAT Law) rather than zero-rated; the exemption covers transactions, including negotiation, concerning payments, transfers and debts. Cross-border B2B services supplied to taxable persons in other EU Member States or third countries fall outside Luxembourg VAT scope under the place-of-supply (reverse charge) rules, provided the supplier holds the customer's valid EU VAT ID or adequate evidence of business status; such services remain subject to the customer's domestic rules and cannot be zero-rated with an input-credit entitlement in Luxembourg.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Single Administrative Document, SAD/ECS) with customs office exit stamp or electronic harmonised export data
Transport documentation (CMR waybill, Bill of Lading, or Air Waybill) evidencing physical removal from the EU

Commercial invoice, sales/export contract, and insurance certificates; payment intermediation records (SWIFT MT103/MT202, bank account statements) proving completed cross-border remittance and consideration received
Inward remittance certificate / EUR1 or movement certificate where preferential origin applies
Customer due-diligence file (KYC/AML) confirming the identity and business status of the overseas recipient for exempt or reverse-charge treatment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may reassess VAT within five years (ten years in cases of fraud or wilful misconduct). Unsubstantiated zero-rating or wrongful exemption is retrospectively clawed back with default interest of 0.8% per month or part-month (Article 87 of the VAT Law), plus fines of EUR 250 to EUR 10,000 per infraction (Article 84). Fraudulent evasion (including falsified export proofs or fictitious cross-border payments) exposes managers to criminal fines up to EUR 10,000 and imprisonment under Articles 84–86 of the VAT Law and Article 60 of the Customs Code; the CSSF revokes the payment-institution licence on adverse findings, and repeat offenders incur a 100% penalty on the differential tax. Anti-abuse provisions (Article 6 of the VAT Law and GAAR in the General Tax Law) disregard artificial arrangements and re-characterise cross-border remittance chains to the taxable destination.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting jointly with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); the Ministry of Finance retains residual licensing and sanctions policy authority. The BCL manages balance-of-payments statistical monitoring and settlement systems (TARGET2-LU), while the CSSF authorizes and supervises payments institutions and credit institutions under the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services and the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: As a Eurozone member with fully liberalized capital movements pursuant to Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls on either current or capital transactions. The euro is a freely convertible floating currency. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, repayment of shareholder loans, and repatriation of liquidation proceeds are unrestricted, subject only to standardized corporate documentation (audited financial statements, withholding tax certificates under Article 147, and the Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends at the applicable 15% domestic rate or reduced treaty rate). No prior Central Bank approval is required for any cross-border transfer exceeding any threshold; however, BCL statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligations apply to financial intermediaries and resident direct investment flows above €12,500.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg maintains no export proceeds surrender regime, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory repatriation timeline for export or service receipts. A remittance agency may invoice and hold foreign currency freely in Luxembourg accounts. Any EUR conversion is driven purely by commercial settlement needs and bank counterparty liquidity, with no government-mandated conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Escrow sub-accounts for remittance settlement pools
Capital Escrow Account / Settlement Nostro Account
CBW Settlement Account and Cash-Pickup Prefunding Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate viability with high regulatory friction. A Luxembourg-authorised Electronic Money Institution (EMI) or Payment Institution (PI) licence (agrément) under the Law of 10 November 2009 is the only permissible legal wrapper for operating the money transmission business; the ISIC 6619 activity is a payment service under Annex I(6) of PSD2 (money remittance) and triggers mandatory CSSF licensing, with initial capital €20,000–€125,000 depending on service scope, plus prudential safeguarding of user funds. Offshore digital EMIs located in third countries cannot lawfully provide remittance services to Luxembourg residents without passporting; a third-country fintech may only act as an unregulated white-label technology provider to the licensed Luxembourg PI, and may not touch customer funds. The CSSF will expect substance: a Luxembourg registered office, one resident Conducting Officer with local AML expertise and adequate script, and auditable transaction monitoring hosted in the EEA.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not formally impose a statutory obligation for all directors to appear physically before the CSSF for payment institution licensing; however, the CSSF conducts an interactive assessment that effectively requires at least the designated Conducting Officer(s) and the beneficial owner to appear in person in Luxembourg for a fit-and-proper interview. For commercial bank account opening, the standard Luxembourg AML/CFT practice (Law of 12 November 2004, Article 3-1, as amended, and CSSF Regulation 12-02) obliges banks to verify the identity of the client and beneficial owner; in practice, all tier-1 Luxembourg banks require a physical meeting at which original passports, proof of address, and the corporate KYC file are presented, although remote video identification is technically admissible under the EBA Guidelines on Customer Due Diligence (EBA/GL/2022/15) if it deploys qualified digital identity verification and liveness detection. For high-risk sectors (money remittance licensed entities), the prevailing market standard is a mandatory on-site visit to the bank's head office in Luxembourg City by at least the legal representative and the AML compliance officer of the SARL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk license classification: the bank perceives consumer remittance as an inherently money-laundering-sensitive operation (FATF Guidance on Money or Value Transfer Services, June 2021).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the CSSF Payment Institution licence with the exact scope; a full regulatory compliance manual including FATF Recommendation 16 Travel Rule implementation; audited transaction monitoring system (e.g., tool-specific thresholds and machine-learning case management report); board-approved AML/CFT risk assessment; evidence that the entity itself is supervised, not an unlicensed agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of the underlying remittance source and destination funds when the ORIGINATING customer is a third-party natural person using cash pickup corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer due diligence (CDD) file for each originator: copy of national ID/passport, proof of income and source of funds (payslips, tax returns), designated-name-only beneficiary data, transaction purpose declaration for each transfer, and a capped transaction matrix (e.g., EUR 1,500 per transaction / 5,000 per month) with automated anomaly alerts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Correspondent and payout sub-agent network risk: the bank is concerned that clearing through external cash-pickup agents overseas may violate sub-contracting rules and the 'correspondent finance' AML framework.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete sub-agent register with signed agency agreements undertaking AML/CFT obligations mirroring the CSSF outsourcing requirements; the CSSF notification file under Circular 22/806 (outsourcing) where applicable; FATF R.15–16 compliant agent-due-diligence evidence; periodic on-site agent audit reports and contractually enforced sanctions screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and country-corridor exposure: bank due diligence flags exposure to high-risk corridors or sanctioned territories through cash pickup locations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time sanction-screening evidence demonstrating coverage of EU consolidated sanctions, OFAC SDN, UNSCR, and local BCL/COMELEC lists; geo-blocking of sanctioned jurisdictions at point-of-origin; corridor risk-rated matrix delisting any wrongdoing financial activities; negative news monitoring and periodic sanctions testing certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or nominee shareholder structure in the Luxembourg SARL with foreign ultimate owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered beneficial owner extract from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) under the Law of 13 January 2019, certified not older than 15 days; unabridged shareholders register with minimum capital proof; original signed resolution of the Board appointing the AML reporting officer; personal KYC and fit-and-proper evidence for each UBO; tax residential certificates and certified passport copies.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: shareholder capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 (or equivalent euro payment via TARGET2-LU) from the parent shareholder's account into the SARL's escrow account held at a Luxembourg bank, with the received wire explicitly tagged 'Direct investment - equity capital' plus the Luxembourg BCL balance-of-payments reporting code for direct investment equity (BOP category EA). The following must accompany the wire: (1) the SARL's Luxembourg registration number (RCS Luxembourg), (2) the UBO/RBE reference, (3) the notarised capital increase deed if it represents a contribution adjusting the registered capital, and (4) the bank's calculation of any withholding tax or exemption claim (for share premium, treatment under Article 15(2) of the Luxembourg withholding tax law). Any loan-based injection requires a written shareholder loan agreement at arm's length, which the Luxembourg bank will treat as a related-party liability subject to thin-capitalization and transfer-pricing documentation; the wire purpose for a loan must be coded 'borrowing – intercompany' to avoid misclassification as equity. The BCL requires monthly balance-of-payments statistical reporting of all such injections above the €12,500 threshold, which is effected by the depositary bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (a) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for EUR-denominated beneficiary disbursements within the EEA; (b) SWIFT MT103 over the TARGET2 and SWIFTNet FIN network for all non-EEA or USD/GBP/CHF payouts, with mandatory originator and beneficiary structured fields required by EU Regulation 2015/847 (information accompanying transfers); (c) commercial letters of credit (LC) issued by the Luxembourg settlement bank for large disbursements against documents, otherwise documentary collection (DP/DA); (d) for cash-pickup corridor clearing, the licensed PI must pre-fund tapped payout correspondents via their nostro accounts at global clearing banks rather than using open correspondent free-float balances. Every outbound disbursement must be linked to the transaction-specific audit trail containing originator name, beneficiary name, amount, and purpose code, and where the payout agent is unlicensed, the PI must be able to prove beneficiary identity verification and sanction screening at the myriad gateways.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forward contracts (plain vanilla, settled T+2 via CLS), permissible as hedging instruments written by any prudentially supervised Luxembourg bank; no exchange-control approval required.
EUR/GBP deliverable FX forward contracts (same framework).
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (CCIRS) for hedging reinvested remittance float or a shareholder loan denominated in a foreign currency.

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) contracts on emerging-market corridor currencies (e.g., EUR/Naira, EUR/PKR, EUR/BDT) executed with an EEA-domiciled counterparty in the offshore NDF market; settlement in EUR is permissible and does not trigger any local exchange controls.

FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) to manage intraday liquidity between the escrow EUR account and the payouts segment accounts, subject to the CSSF's prudent-hedging classification only so that no speculative position is created.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, profit-and-loss account and notes) approved by the shareholders and filed with the Luxembourg trade and companies register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) - Administration du Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval no later than six months after the financial year-end; filing with the RCS within one month of approval and in all cases before expiry of seven months from the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-publication of annual accounts is an offence under Luxembourg company law; the RCS court may impose fines, the records are struck off if persistently missing, and managers may be held personally liable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return incorporating the municipal business tax and net wealth tax declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SARL, the annual return is due by 30 April of the following year; mandatory electronic filing and the tax authority's practice of granting extensions apply to e-filed returns.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and late payment trigger late-filing penalties and monthly late-payment interest of 0.5%; continued non-filing enables the tax administration to issue an ex officio assessment and enforce collection through distraint.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CSSF annual prudential, financial and AML/CTF compliance file for the licensed cross-border remittance and payment-services entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual audited financial statements must be submitted within six months of the financial year-end; prudential and AML/CTF reporting must follow the CSSF circular deadlines applicable to payment institutions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing or late CSSF filings constitute regulatory breaches punishable by administrative fines and enforcement measures, including suspension or withdrawal of the payment-services licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-ownership register accuracy declaration and update file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing on incorporation; update filing within one month after any change in the UBO structure; annual verification by the board before approval of the annual accounts (no separate annual UBO re-filing).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain accurate UBO information is an AML/CTF compliance offence carrying administrative fines and potential criminal penalties; continuing default may expose the SARL and managers to enforcement and strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is compulsory for a Luxembourg payment institution holding a CSSF licence irrespective of size; otherwise a SARL must appoint a réviseur d'entreprises when it exceeds two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average employees 50; the audit may also be triggered by a creditor or shareholder request under the law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register, bookkeeping and annual accounts, as amended, implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be used if voluntarily elected or required for the consolidated group accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO confirmation declaration exists under Luxembourg RBE law. The SARL must file any UBO change within one month of the triggering event, including any transfer of shares; before the annual accounts are approved, the board must reconcile the RBE declaration against the share register and record the verification in the minutes.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City aggregate for tax year 2024: 17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box 80% exemption reducing effective rate on qualifying IP income to approximately 4.99%; R&D tax credit; participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains; notional interest deduction (subject to conditions)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulirc 103 (Déclaration pour l’impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) including integrated municipal business tax declaration; filed electronically via the Luxembourg direct tax e-filing portal MyTax (also accepted through accredited eCDF agents)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be filed no later than 31 May following the fiscal year-end; the Luxembourg tax administration generally permits an extended filing date to 31 December for taxpayers filing online or represented by a registered tax adviser

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: registered company name, legal form (SARL), RCS registration number, LEI (ELF Code), registered office address, and business license reference
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box is completed by the resident Luxembourg SARL; non-resident shareholders have no filing duty on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year commencement and closing dates, plus the immediately preceding fiscal year-end for comparatives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same as Box 1a; only a Luxembourg tax-resident entity files this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit and loss reconciliation: net commercial profit or loss per audited statutory accounts before tax additions and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) must file a separate non-resident box set; the SARL return is not used for PE-only positions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and disallowed items: non-deductible expenses including 30% EBITDA interest limitation add-back, fines, gifts, excessive remuneration, and withholding tax recoveries
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All add-backs are computed at the level of the SARL and reported by its managing directors; non-resident shareholders cannot amend these lines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income: participation exemption dividends (subject to 10% holding threshold and 12-month minimum holding) and 80% IP box exemption on qualifying net intellectual property income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The exemption forms are signed by the SARL tax representative; non-resident owners claiming DTA relief separately must attach Form 22 and tax residence certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward used in the current year, against the unlimited statutory carryforward pool
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the SARL may utilise its own carried-forward losses; losses of non-resident shareholders or affiliates are not reportable on this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income after add-backs and deductions; this is the base for CIT and the solidarity surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxable base belongs to the SARL; non-resident shareholders' income is not co-mingled on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax base: commercial profit adjusted for interest add-backs and other specific commercial tax additions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The municipal business tax is imposed on the Luxembourg commercial activity of the SARL; non-resident passive shareholders have no municipal tax filing duty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate income tax at 17%, solidarity surcharge at 7% of CIT, and municipal business tax at the applicable communal rate (e.g., 6.75% in Luxembourg City)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This line is the final tax computation of the SARL; any withholding tax on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders is addressed in the annual withholding tax regime, not this return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic penalty of EUR 250; continued non-filing may give rise to a 10% increase in assessed taxes, monthly late payment interest at 0.8%, and, in case of intentional concealment, criminal fines and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% under Luxembourg domestic law; reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the parent holds at least 10% for an uninterrupted 12-month period; treaty rates commonly 5% for substantial direct holdings and 10-15% for portfolio holdings
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver to the Luxembourg paying agent / SARL a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) and complete Luxembourg withholding tax form (Form 22 or equivalent) before the payment date. If relief is not applied at source, the recipient can file a refund claim with the Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration) within the statutory limitation period, generally five years from the end of the calendar year in which the tax was withheld. The SARL must retain proper documentation proving beneficial ownership and the arm's-length nature of the distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes 0% withholding tax on outbound royalty and interest payments to non-resident beneficial owners, provided the amounts are at arm's length and not recharacterised as constructive dividends. Treaty relief is generally unnecessary because there is no domestic source tax; where a DTA is nevertheless invoked, the same TRC and Form 22 procedure applies for procedural certainty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where the Luxembourg SARL's related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 in aggregate in a fiscal year (goods, services, intangibles, and financial transactions). A Master File is required where the worldwide group's consolidated annual revenue reaches at least EUR 750,000,000. These thresholds are expressed in EUR, the local currency of Luxembourg.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no separate Economic Substance Regulations statute equivalent to Cayman/BVI; however, the substance doctrine is embedded through the substance-over-form principle, the case-law-derived 'fraude à la loi' abuse-of-law doctrine, the EU ATAD GAAR, and, for this regulated sector, the CSSF licensing requirements under the law of 10 November 2009 on payment services, which mandate physical presence, local staffing, operational governance, and genuine decision-making power in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal Payment Service Activity / Unlicensed Remittance Business
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating cross-border money transmission and SWIFT/cash-pickup clearing rails for expatriate-worker remittances without a valid Luxembourg payment institution licence from the CSSF or without an available exemption under the Luxembourg law of 10 November 2009 (PSD2 as transposed)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to EUR 5,000,000 and/or imprisonment of 1 to 5 years; administrative sanctions by the CSSF including cessation orders, prohibition of management, withdrawal of licence, and fines up to 10% of gross annual turnover or EUR 5,000,000, whichever is higher
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be declared jointly and severally liable for corporate debts and damages, subjected to asset freezes and travel bans, disqualified from corporate management, and, in aggravated cases, sentenced to imprisonment for operating an unlicensed regulated payment business.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting fee income, foreign-exchange gains, or float investment income; falsifying books and records; or disguising shareholder distributions as deductible expenses to reduce Luxembourg corporate income tax and municipal business tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of omitted income, a tax increase of up to 10% for undisclosed profits, monthly late payment interest at 0.8%, criminal fines, and imprisonment up to 5 years; the limitation period for fraudulent non-declaration is extended to 10 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve false tax returns face criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, and civil liability for the unpaid tax damages under the Luxembourg law on commercial companies; the court may order travel bans and freezing of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive management fees, interest, commissions, or royalties to a foreign related parent or affiliate above arm's length, or failing to prepare and keep the Local File when the EUR 1,000,000 related-party transaction threshold is exceeded
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment increasing the Luxembourg taxable base, disallowance of excessive expenses, recharacterisation of the excess as a dividend subject to 15% Luxembourg withholding tax (unless a DTA reduces the rate), monthly late-payment interest at 0.8%, and penalties; treaty benefits may be denied under GAAR or fraud situations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve non-arm's-length transactions can be held jointly and severally liable for the resulting tax and penalties, prosecuted for tax fraud, and prohibited from holding management positions in regulated financial entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Fraude à la Loi / GAAR
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Luxembourg SARL as a conduit without genuine staff, premises, local decision-making, or operational control, solely to obtain treaty/WHT benefits or to create artificial cross-border payment rails without economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of Luxembourg treaty benefits, reallocation of profits to the place of effective management, recovery of unpaid 15% withholding tax on deemed dividends, addition of late payment interest and penalty, and administrative dissolution or licence revocation in regulated sectors
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for tax liabilities caused by the abusive structure, held civilly liable for restitution to the tax authority, banned from serving as directors, and subject to criminal imprisonment for complicity in tax fraud or money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Compliance Failure and Money Laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to conduct adequate KYC/CDD, ignoring beneficial-owner identification, not filing suspicious transaction reports with the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF), or knowingly using remittance rails to launder dirty money or evade sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF administrative fines of up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; criminal fines and imprisonment of up to 5 years for laundering the proceeds of crime; freezing of funds, seizure of assets, withdrawal of the payment institution licence, and publication of sanctioning decisions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally exposed to criminal imprisonment, fines, asset freezes, travel bans, and professional disqualification; they may also be jointly and severally liable to civil claimants for economic losses caused by the AML breaches.
